evidence_use.operator: arithmetic means and sample SDs on complete endpoint pairs
evidence_use.population: 12 adult men aged 35-55 with abdominal overweight/obesity; fasting measurements before/after 3 days at approximately 50% usual energy intake; no control arm.
evidence_use.measurement: Units specified per endpoint; serum leptin is raw ng/mL, not a log transformation
evidence_use.reason: Use rounded arithmetic means and sample SDs as plug-in population marginal moments with analytic lognormal conversion. Raw units are retained, including raw leptin. These target-derived reconstruction inputs provide no independent validation of means, pairing, change SDs or change correlations. Cohort moments fluctuate; shape, rounding uncertainty and marginal-parameter uncertainty remain assumed or unmodeled.

evidence_use.population: 12 adult men aged 35-55 with abdominal overweight/obesity; fasting measurements before/after 3 days at approximately 50% usual energy intake; no control arm.
evidence_use.reason: Use the paired visit design, population description and exact complete-pair counts; scale counts by requested persons. All four endpoint pairs are complete here. No control arm or unprovided age, adiposity or energy-intake covariates are fabricated. The short interval makes persistent person factors a reasonable sensitivity assumption but does not identify their magnitude.

components.name: raw_positive_marginals
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Same-population A0 reconstruction. For each mean m and SD s, use log variance log(1+(s/m)^2) and log mean log(m)-log_variance/2. Lognormal shape is assumed; arithmetic population moments equal the supplied plug-in values, while sample moments fluctuate. No exact row or marginal matching is performed.

components.name: dependence_sensitivity_set
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Each latent standard normal is a sum of independent standard-normal common person, endpoint person, common visit and endpoint visit factors with square-root variance weights. The three weight rows are (0.20,0.70,0,0.10), (0.20,0.30,0,0.50), and (0.20,0.30,0.35,0.15). Every row sums to one, giving a positive-semidefinite joint model. All weights are chosen assumptions, not source estimates. Common visit factors are independent between pre and post and shared across endpoints within visit. They may represent shared physiological state or measurement-episode effects, which the packet cannot distinguish.

components.name: counts_keys_randomness
components.source_to_target_assumptions: Each complete-pair count is round(endpoint_n*n/packet_n). Generalized missing pairs are randomly placed without replacement independently by endpoint, an unvalidated MCAR convention; this packet has no missing pairs. Keys are new and include scenario, seed and row. Only local np.random.default_rng(seed) is used; evidence is not mutated. Output order is the supplied paired-wide schema.
